title_translated: 面向儿童语音的边缘音素识别：基于年龄感知的训练方法
summary_translated: 由于训练数据稀缺及儿童语音的独特特征，从儿童语音中检测音素历来困难。在一次音素检测竞赛中，我们发现训练一个轻量级模型同时预测学习者的年龄和音素序列，使得一个9400万参数的模型在目标DrivenData分布上超越了WavLM Large模型（3.17亿参数），并以约0.04的词错误率（CER）接近竞赛集成模型（其参数量为本模型的90倍）。这促成了PhonemeTrainer应用的开发，可在大多数现代智能手机上运行。这将最终实现针对儿童语音的更好自动语音识别（ASR）和发音辅助应用，同时具备边缘计算带来的隐私与合规优势。

summary: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) aggregates heterogeneous preferences into a single reward model, assuming preference homogeneity. When preferences are heterogeneous, this aggregation induces a procedural fairness failure where majority preference groups dominate reward learning while minority preferences are systematically under-represented. This work defines procedural fairness in alignment as preserving distinct preference signals during reward modeling and shows that standard RLHF violates this via preference averaging. Preference-Aware RLHF (PA-RLHF) is introduced, separating optimization across preference modes at the reward learning stage. In a controlled setting, PA-RLHF improves overall alignment accuracy from 46.9% to 67.9% and reduces the fairness gap between best and worst aligned groups from 15.9 to 9.6 percentage points. These results show that procedural fairness failures in alignment can arise from structural design choices in reward learning, even in controlled, noise-free settings, with direct implications for large language models and agentic systems, where biased reward models can compound inequities across sequential decisions.
title: Procedural Fairness Failures in RLHF from Preference Averaging
comment: 4 pages, Accepted at the ICLR 2026 Workshop on Algorithmic Fairness Across Alignment Procedures and Agentic Systems (AFAA)
title_translated: 从偏好平均中产生的RLHF程序公平性失效
summary_translated: 基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）将异质性偏好聚合为单一奖励模型，假设偏好同质性。当偏好存在异质性时，这种聚合会导致程序公平性失效，即多数偏好群体主导奖励学习，而少数偏好被系统性地低估。本文将对齐中的程序公平性定义为在奖励建模过程中保留不同的偏好信号，并表明标准RLHF因偏好平均而违反了这一原则。为此提出了感知偏好的RLHF（PA-RLHF），在奖励学习阶段分离不同偏好模式的优化。在受控环境中，PA-RLHF将整体对齐准确率从46.9%提升至67.9%，并将最佳与最差对齐群体之间的公平差距从15.9个百分点降至9.6个百分点。结果表明，即使在无噪声的受控设置下，奖励学习的结构性设计选择也可能引发对齐中的程序公平性失效，这对大语言模型和代理系统具有直接意义，因为有偏的奖励模型可能在序列决策中加剧不平等。

summary: LLM recommenders for top-$K$ item suggestion regularly emit titles outside the target catalog. Prior audits measure this as a binary out-of-domain rate; none ask whether the model knew it was hallucinating. We jointly audit hallucination rate (OOD@10) and verbalized-confidence calibration (ECE, Brier, reliability) for four zero-shot LLM recommenders from four independent vendors (Mistral Large, Llama-3.3-70B, GPT-OSS-120B, Claude Sonnet 4.6), not grounded or fine-tuned systems, across three catalogs (MovieLens-25M, Amazon Reviews 2023 Toys, Yelp Open Dataset), stratified by item popularity. Hallucination is catalog-dependent (0--0.2\% on MovieLens, 4.5--8.3\% on Amazon, 2.2--8.4\% on Yelp), but verbalized confidence is materially miscalibrated even when hallucination is zero (ECE up to 0.223 on MovieLens despite 0\% OOD). All four LLMs are systematically \emph{under}-confident across all twelve cells, verbalizing a mean of 67--86 on items they recommend with 92--100\% accuracy. This is the opposite of the over-confidence usually emphasized in LLM-hallucination work. The under-confidence is best read as an \emph{elicitation mismatch}: ``Just Ask'' elicits a generic recommendation-quality rating, not a catalog-membership probability. A conformal abstention threshold over verbalized confidence reduces hallucination by at most 0.7\,pp across $α\in \{.05, .10, .15, .20\}$, at 4--21\,pp of coverage cost: the under-confident channel cannot separate correct items from hallucinations, so the threshold mostly removes correct items. We recommend that audits of LLM recommenders report calibration alongside OOD, and use catalog-anchored elicitation rather than generic confidence prompts.
title: Do LLM Recommenders Know When They're Hallucinating? Auditing Confidence Calibration in Catalog Faithfulness
title_translated: LLM推荐器是否知道它们在幻觉？关于目录忠实度中置信度校准的审计
summary_translated: 用于Top-K项目推荐的大型语言模型经常生成目标目录外的标题。以往的审计将其视为二元的域外率；但无人询问模型是否意识到自己在幻觉。我们联合审计了四种独立供应商（Mistral Large、Llama-3.3-70B、GPT-OSS-120B、Claude Sonnet 4.6）的零样本LLM推荐器在三个目录（MovieLens-25M、Amazon Reviews 2023 Toys、Yelp Open Dataset）上的幻觉率（OOD@10）和口头置信度校准情况（ECE、Brier、可靠性），并按项目流行度分层。幻觉率依赖于目录（MovieLens上为0–0.2%，Amazon上为4.5–8.3%，Yelp上为2.2–8.4%），但即使在幻觉率为零的情况下，口头置信度也严重校准不当（MovieLens上ECE高达0.223）。所有四个LLM在全部十二个场景中均系统性地表现出置信度不足，其推荐的项目准确率达92–100%时，口头置信度平均仅为67–86。这与通常强调的LLM过度自信现象相反。这种置信度不足可解读为一种‘诱发不匹配’：‘只需提问’会诱发通用推荐质量评分，而非目录成员概率。基于口头置信度的共形弃权阈值最多仅能降低0.7个百分点的幻觉率，代价为4–21个百分点的覆盖率损失：由于置信度不足的通道无法区分正确项与幻觉项，该阈值主要剔除了正确项。我们建议在审计LLM推荐器时应同时报告校准情况，并采用以目录为中心的诱导方式，而非通用置信度提示。

summary: Large language models are increasingly used to read markets, assess risk, and allocate capital. However, reported results for LLM trading agents can be inflated by look-ahead leakage, optimistic execution, and risk mandates that are described but not enforced. We present OpenPM, an auditable point-in-time evaluation framework for LLM portfolio-management agents. In OpenPM, an agent manages a \$1M long-only book over the S\&P 500 universe using market data at five-minute intervals. Every record visible to the agent must be available at the decision time. Natural-language risk mandates are converted into typed constraints and enforced on the executed portfolio. Each run produces audit artifacts, including a contamination certificate, a cost-sensitivity curve, and a constraint-adherence report. We also build a reference agent named the tiered allocator, where typed analysts score candidates, a constructor LLM proposes weights, and a deterministic critic guarantees feasibility. We isolate constructor behavior by capturing analyst evidence once and replaying it across constructor models. In our short-window case study, stronger constructors show modest and model-dependent gains over equal weighting on the same pool, but analyst quality matters more than constructor choice, and turnover is the main cost driver. All returns are upper bounds on a single frozen window without market impact, not validated alpha.
title: OpenPM: Auditable Point-in-Time Evaluation for LLM Portfolio-Management Agents
title_translated: OpenPM：面向LLM投资组合管理代理的可审计时点评估
summary_translated: 大型语言模型越来越多地被用于市场阅读、风险评估和资本配置。然而，LLM交易代理报告的结果可能因前瞻泄露、乐观执行以及未实际执行的风险指令而被夸大。我们提出OpenPM，一种面向LLM投资组合管理代理的可审计时点评估框架。在OpenPM中，代理使用每五分钟更新的市场数据，在标普500范围内管理一个100万美元的多头投资组合。代理可见的每一笔记录必须在决策时刻可用。自然语言形式的风险指令被转换为类型化约束并在执行后的投资组合中强制执行。每次运行都会生成审计材料，包括污染证书、成本敏感性曲线和约束遵守报告。我们还构建了一个名为分层分配器的基准代理，其中类型化分析师评分候选项，构造型LLM提出权重，确定性批评者保证可行性。通过仅捕获一次分析师证据并在多个构造模型间重放，我们隔离了构造器的行为。在我们的短窗口案例研究中，更强的构造器在相同池中相对于等权重带来适度且模型依赖的收益，但分析师质量比构造器选择更重要，换手率是主要成本驱动因素。所有回报均为单个冻结窗口内的上限，未考虑市场冲击，非验证的阿尔法。

summary: Designing autonomous agents that effectively assist human teams hinges on understanding team dynamics, often without task specific knowledge. We present TRIBE, a domain independent approach that reveals team behavioral dynamics invisible to traditional performance metrics. We show that communication patterns can categorize teams into performance predictive behavioral tribes, as early as 10% into the task, enabling timely interventions. We test TRIBE on four diverse datasets and demonstrate that communication patterns predict team performance while the prediction strength varies by the degree a task structure allows for behavioral freedom. Our temporal analysis reveals that AI agents significantly alter team behavioral trajectories while human advisors align with natural dynamics, and that teams maintain behavioral flexibility throughout collaboration. Further, we compare TRIBE to Llama and optimize the pipeline, achieving significant speedup with performance improvement.
title: TRIBE: Predicting Team Performance via Communication Behavior Ensembles
title_translated: TRIBE：通过通信行为集成预测团队绩效
summary_translated: 设计能够有效辅助人类团队的自主智能体，关键在于理解团队动态，而无需特定任务知识。我们提出TRIBE，一种领域无关的方法，揭示传统绩效指标无法察觉的团队行为动态。我们发现，通信模式可以将团队分类为具有绩效预测能力的行为部落，最早可在任务进行10%时实现，从而支持及时干预。我们在四个多样化数据集上测试TRIBE，证明通信模式能够预测团队绩效，且预测强度随任务结构允许的行为自由度而变化。时间分析显示，AI代理显著改变了团队行为轨迹，而人类顾问则与自然动态保持一致，且团队在整个协作过程中维持行为灵活性。此外，我们将TRIBE与Llama对比并优化流程，实现了显著的速度提升和性能改进。

summary: Frontier language models are trained using distinct data, objectives, and safety pipelines. Whether these differences produce measurably different behaviors under explicit steering pressure remains underexplored. This study evaluates behavioral steerability across six frontier models from six developers using 300 paired base and steered items over three categories: values-conflict, reasoning-elicitation, and reasoning-suppression (plus 40 validation items). All six models act as blind peer judges and classify every response based on fixed behavioral rubrics. The resulting 24,480 judgments are scored by leave-one-out consensus. We find that models differ not just in how much steering shifts their behavior but in what kind (mode) of response they give, and some response modes appear in only one or two of them. GPT-5 deflects requests to disclose its reasoning while leaving its answer intact (99% vs. 0% for all other models). Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5 resist explicit suppression instructions and in different ways. Using Llama as the open-weight model, we trace the largest behavioral split to its internals. A linear probe decodes the behavior from the residual stream at 0.87 held-out accuracy while injecting that direction during generation drives the behavior from 0% to 86% across an intervention sweep. Every finding holds under both a token-budget remediation and a control experiment with a hypothesis-blind judgment prompt.
title: Divergent Response Modes in Frontier Language Models Under Steering Pressure
title_translated: 前沿语言模型在引导压力下的分歧响应模式
summary_translated: 前沿语言模型使用不同的数据、目标和安全管道进行训练。这些差异在显式引导压力下是否会产生可测量的不同行为仍缺乏深入探索。本研究评估了来自六家开发者的六个前沿模型在三种类别下的行为可引导性：价值观冲突、推理激发和推理抑制（另加40个验证项），共使用300对基础与引导样本。所有六个模型均作为盲眼同行评审员，根据固定的行为评分标准对每个响应进行分类。由此产生的24,480条判断通过留一法共识进行评分。我们发现，各模型不仅在引导对其行为的影响程度上存在差异，而且在响应模式（类型）上也不同，某些响应模式仅出现在一个或两个模型中。GPT-5在拒绝披露其推理过程的同时保持答案不变（99% vs. 所有其他模型的0%）。Claude Opus 4.7和GPT-5以不同方式抵抗明确的抑制指令。使用Llama作为开源权重模型，我们追踪到最大的行为分歧源于其内部机制。线性探测器在残差流中以0.87的保留准确率解码行为，而在生成过程中注入该方向可使行为从0%提升至86%。所有发现均在令牌预算修复和假设盲评提示控制实验下成立。
